excludedAreas: PDF metadata title and preface say issue 2 / second issue, while the final printed footer says issue 4_07-15. Identify the source by document number, July 2015, panel scope and SHA256; preserve both issue descriptions.

Full-size operator instructions repeatedly use loop 1-2 despite p22 describing cards 1-4 and up to six for VIG1-72. Generic appendix selectors allow 1-8. The fictional commissioned site has only loops 1 and 2. No claim that two or eight is the hardware capacity of the selected 4/6-loop panel.

Operator device range is 1-200; generic appendix parameter boxes use 1-207. Operator forms use the documented 1-200 range and validate against the fictional installed devices. Extended/reserved addresses are not assumed.

Repair p38 says F1 Test/Eng, contradicting the visible F4 top-level mapping, and says F1 Loop after UserCode where PIN-change p21 specifies F1 NewPass. Repair is reference-only, with no fabricated exact button lesson.

The narrative on p81 abbreviates and orders the selectors differently from the complete p105 diagram. A manufacturer training slide independently shows both Test selections followed by On/Off, direct zone-number entry and Enter. Use the complete 2015 p105 branch and document the p103 training-slide corroboration. There is no additional Zone function-key selection or Loop step. The profile remains classic EN54 (V4), MCC/MCB V4.53+, and has not been validated against a physical panel.
Operator p26 says choose FARE with F4 after cycling <etc>; the generic control map positions FARE before <etc>. FARE output On/Off is a source-reference branch.

Operator p28 says Aux Rly is F2 after three <etc> presses. p27 says FPE is F2; the appendix page places FARE,FPE,AuxRly in that order. Show appendix order in the reference map; Aux Rly operation remains reference-only.

July 2015 operator text describes individual MCP sensing disablement but does not explicitly state MCP behaviour when a zone is disabled. An older 1999 manual differs in scope and is not silently imported. The zone-disable lesson uses Zone 2, with no MCP. Full MCP-in-zone behaviour requires panel-specific confirmation.
The p9 indicator table calls the delay-block row Sounder; the physical-face illustration labels it Delay. Use the physical-face Delay label and explain its delay-block meaning.
The face artwork repeats 30 in the 17-32 zone row. Render the normal continuous zone numbers 1-32 and disclose the artwork discrepancy here.

Within the FPE procedure one line says FARE while its headings, choice and confirmation all say FPE. Keep FPE terminology based on the explicit heading, selector and confirmation; FPE operation is reference-only.
View IO label uses F2 Device; Edit IO label explicitly uses F3 Device. Preserve each printed route rather than standardising the two.
Display/Print selection is skipped if the printer is absent or switched off. Start with a fitted printer switched off and dynamically include output selection when switched on.

AL1, AL2a, AL2b and AL3 have different visibility. Compact VA, D1 voice, SD card, radio, network and Freeblock conditions introduce further branches. Customer routes remain interactive. Only the sourced zone walk-test engineering branch is added behind a distinct fictional practice credential. Other engineering and fitted-option operations remain references.

The keyboard includes Insert, Delete, Shift and cursor keys; the operator text does not fully specify cursor editing semantics. FINDR uses a documented training text editor and enforces source label limits; no claim of byte-for-byte firmware editing behaviour.
Display test and Zone Test have approximate documented durations; real alarm behaviour depends on commissioning. Use training timing and distinguish rising hint tones from physical panel sounds.

The source documents the clock-field order and controls but does not specify a permitted year range. The practice date editor uses 2000-2099 as an explicit FINDR calendar limit, not a claimed Gent hardware or firmware limit.

Params, Cancel and Quit exist in the documentation, but their exact function-key positions are not established independently for every form. Live forms show individually verified function-key positions. The p105 zone-entry row explicitly supplies F2 Enter, F3 Cancel and F4 Quit. FINDR clearing an uncommitted draft on Cancel is a declared editing convention; it never ends a committed test selection. Additional Params behaviour remains reference-only.

The source allows zone ranges and describes additional installation-dependent output inhibition. FINDR exercises one installed zone at a time; external plant, delay blocks, network functions and real protective outputs are not simulated. An active test input must be restored before Off; that transition restriction and concise confirmation wording are FINDR policies. Teach the physical start/end key path, five-second test cycle, persistent Test indication and explicit restoration without claiming full firmware or external-output fidelity. The Cancel key clears only an uncommitted FINDR draft.
